pains  in  limbs,  which  often  cause  crying  and  are  fre-
quently followed  by  cedematous  swelling  of  whole  body;
extremely  tardy  desquamation.

ELAPS  CORALLINUS.

The  Coral  Viper.  Elapidse.

The  poison  of  the  Brazilian  Coral  Snake  was  first  proved  by  Mure,  who  used
the  3d  trit.  of  the  venom,  and  again  by  Lippe,  on  a  woman  who  took  4t]i  dilution.

The  poison  is  pressed  from  the  venom  sac  of  the  living  reptile,  and  triturated
with  sugar  of  milk.  The  cures  reported  by  S.  B.  Higgins,  however,  were  made
with  a  preparation  made  from  the  gall  of  the  snake,  Fel  Elaps  Corallinus.  Higgins,
N.  A.  J.  H.,  V.  24,  p.  115,  remarks:  "The  pathogenetic  action  of  Fel  E.  C.  is  in
many  respects  similar  to  Elaps  Corallinus,  but  in  almost  every  case  its  action  will
probably  be  found  to  be  much  more  strongly  marked  than  that  of  the  latter."
These  symptoms  are  marked .
